message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora (felids) and Perissodactyla (equids), respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade that contains all placental mammals (Eutheria). This ancestor lived roughly 100 million years ago, during the early Cretaceous, before the diversification of the major placental orders.
